Similarly to the uncontrolled case, vehicles returned are still assigned EVSE rating based on arrival SOC. However, contrary to uncontrolled case, here the EVSE set points are adjusted in real time, such that the total load (facility plus EV) sits below the grid ceiling. Results from the simulation are presented in Figure 13, while aggregated results are in Table 5. Figure 14 shows how the addition of DER enabled the site controller to provide significantly more power to the EVSE, while the BESS almost entirely avoided exceeding the distribution ceiling through peak shaving. The oscillations in net power demand are due to the delay between the measurement of the current EVSE set points and the update and implementation of the next dispatch points through the feedback controller, hence the need for a “buffer” region, here set above 1,750 kW. Shown in Table 6, this SCM strategy and DER configuration resulted in 10% of charging sessions interrupted with an average 13% SOC deficit, which is comparable to the baseline scenario, and also in a peak load of 2.2 MW, which would likely avoid infrastructure upgrades.
